answer: A Sybil-resistant agent economy can require each identity to lock a refundable deposit that only unlocks after a long horizon of honest work, so a fake army must fund every copy. Newcomers start with tiny task limits and earn larger jobs only through verified completions, so trust grows in a slow spiral rather than by declaration. A bridge service then vouches for proven agents across markets, but slashes the deposit of any identity caught cheating, making mass fakery cost more than it can ever earn.
